fixed.how: New StatusBoard (packages/runtime/src/loop/status-board.ts) plus status-board-words.ts. The issue is titled 'Forerunner status: <project>', its body starts with the marker `<!-- forerunner:status v1 key=K -->`, it carries the label forerunner:status, and it is pinned while fewer than three issues are pinned. Each writer keeps one comment marked `<!-- forerunner:status-writer v1 key=K writer=W -->` with the header `**<agent> (Forerunner)** · <login> · updated …` and edits it in place (commentOnIssue once, updateIssueComment after that). The runner hooks taskStarted, taskBoundary and sessionEnded drive it. The pending write is stored in <projectsRoot>/<id>/status-issue.json, so no migration is needed. compose wires the board when the runtime can reach GitHub and is not the cloud runner, and registers the device row in that case.

fixed.problem: Someone editing, deleting or closing the status on GitHub could leave it wrong or duplicated.

fixed.how: The board compares the comment's body with the text it last sent (`sent`). If someone changed it, the person gets one Update (commentChangedUpdate) and the writer's text goes back on the next write. A deleted comment is written again. A closed issue stops the writes and says closedIssueSentence; the board never reopens it. A deleted issue gets one new issue and one Update (issueDeletedUpdate). When two writers open an issue at the same time, the one with the higher number closes its own with 'Closed: #N is this project's status issue.'.

new_problems: On the two-person bench both agents are named 'Alice', so both comment headers read '**Alice (Forerunner)** · ada' and '**Alice (Forerunner)** · bob' (see /tmp/frbench/fix-w8-status-write/steps/after-status-issue.txt). On the stand-in GitHub, issue numbers and PR numbers share one sequence (as on GitHub), so the first status issue is often #1 before any task PR. That is right for GitHub, but some older tests assume PR #1.

The repository guide's statusIssueTitle text is written unredacted, while the board redacts the project name with safeLine/redactQuoted. A project name holding an email or figure would differ between the guide and the issue title (w8-repo-guide owner).

Before the first session, the Docs Status row shows the 'missing' badge beside 'Status on GitHub: the status issue is written when a task starts or a session ends.'. The badge is the docs file's state, but it reads as if the status issue were missing.
